item.text: {"question_id":"4B.5","answer":"The 2023 record shows inclusion-oriented institutional appointments and restructuring, including the first Indigenous leaders heading the Indigenous affairs agency and Ministry of Indigenous Peoples, creation or restoration of bodies for Indigenous policy, LGBTQI+ rights, women, racial equality, and human rights, and reopened civil-society space (BATCH-0001-E011, BATCH-0001-E036, BATCH-0001-E037, BATCH-0016-E003). These actions support pluralistic representation and institution-building, but they do not by themselves establish politically neutral appointments, civil-service neutrality, or neutral day-to-day administration. The record also contains qualifying evidence: Lula selected an attorney general outside the prosecutors’ shortlist, departing from a traditional independence-preserving practice (BATCH-0007-E007). In the GSI, the Lula-appointed chief initially retained several senior personnel inherited from the prior administration, removed nine people at first, and later changed roughly 250 personnel; he retrospectively acknowledged that retaining some inherited personnel may have been an error and ordered inquiries into alleged failures (BATCH-0020-E023, BATCH-0020-E027, BATCH-0020-E030). Those accounts are contested and do not establish that the retained officials were politically disloyal, that Lula directly directed the staffing decisions, or that the government imposed systematic loyalty tests, party capture, intimidation, or a personality cult. The supplied evidence therefore supports a mixed but limited assessment of administrative neutrality, with stronger evidence for representative institution-building than for comprehensive
